intended_object: The category of DG local systems on a space B that may not be path-connected, with one basepoint b_c chosen in each path component c. Its objects are families (𝓕_c) where each 𝓕_c is a right DG module over the Moore loop chain algebra C_*(Ω_{b_c} B; R), and morphisms are taken componentwise. This follows Barraud–Damian–Humilière–Oancea; I inferred it from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is the dependent product, over path components c : ZerothHomotopy B, of the categories DGLocalSystem B (β.point c) R. `PathComponentBasepoints` is a section of the projection to path components, so each β.point c lies in the component c. The `Category` instance declared right after is `CategoryTheory.pi`, so morphisms are componentwise. This is exactly the source's definition for spaces that are not path-connected.

Basing the loop space at b_c inside all of B is correct, because based loops stay inside the path component of their basepoint. Degenerate cases also come out right: if B is empty, the index type is empty and the product is the terminal category with one object.

The generality is natural: any topological space and any commutative ring R. Mathlib has no notion of DG local systems or Moore loop chain algebras, so there is no Mathlib counterpart, and the definition is not too narrow.
